title: Debt Atlas
provenance_note: Reconstructed 2026-09-04. The original delivery referenced data/meta.json from index.html and from BUILD-PLAN.md but did not include it, so the page could not load. This file was authored to close that gap. It contains no figures, only cadence, endpoints and schema, so nothing here overrides a researched value.
authoring_rules: Every value carries value, unit, as_of, confidence, source and source_url. A value missing as_of or source_url renders with a visible warning rather than rendering clean.
confidence is one of reported (filed or official), estimate (third-party reconstruction), projection (a model). It drives colour and hatching, so mislabelling is a correctness bug.
No figure is typed into markup. Prose interpolates from the data layer.
A disputed figure gets a sibling disputed field rather than being overwritten.

source_url is stored in canonical form: where a publisher serves the same page at more than one path, use the one its own canonical tag names. The sources list also folds URLs sharing a host and final path segment, keeping the shortest, so a variant that slips in does not list the same article twice.

confidence_levels.reported: Filed with a regulator or published by the issuing institution.
confidence_levels.projection: Output of a model, not an observation.

files.label: GDP denominators and the CAD/USD rate
files.note: US GDP from FRED. Canada GDP is an IMF full-year estimate; StatCan WDS can replace it once vector IDs are settled. FX_CAD_USD lives here so the page can show which rate produced a converted bar.

files.label: US federal debt level, ratio, projections
files.note: Level from Treasury Fiscal Data, ratio from FRED GFDEGDQ188S. Projections are institutional models and are never touched by the updater.

files.label: US and Canadian household balance sheets
files.note: NY Fed publishes XLSX roughly six weeks after quarter end: parse the workbook, never scrape the HTML. StatCan National Balance Sheet Accounts roughly ten weeks after.

files.label: AI corporate debt across three measures
files.cadence: quarterly on earnings, plus ad hoc
files.note: SEC filings, ratings notes and press reporting. Needs something that can read, not something that can poll. Carries last_reviewed; the page shows staleness past the threshold below.

files.label: Telecom analogue and leading indicators
files.note: Historical. Changes only when the analysis changes.

files.label: Machine-fetched long time series
files.note: Thirteen FRED series, about 2,900 observations. Rewritten wholesale by the updater and never hand-edited, which is why it is kept out of the curated set.

files.label: US and Canadian recession bands
files.note: Vendored from econ-core, not authored here, and never edited in place: re-run econ-core's vendor.sh to update it. US bands derive mechanically from FRED USREC (NBER); Canadian bands are the C.D. Howe Institute Business Cycle Council chronology, which has no API. One dataset shared by every site in the collection, so two pages cannot disagree about when a recession was.

staleness.note: ai-capital.json and cycles.json cannot be automated. Once last_reviewed exceeds this many days the page says so. Honest staleness beats a number that looks fresh because a cron touched the file.

updater.note: A fetched value differing from the stored one by more than max_change_percent is logged and not written. These series do not move that fast, so a large jump means an API change, a units change, or a bad parse. The updater never creates a value; a new series is a human decision.
guardrails: Existing values only. The updater cannot create a series.
Only value and as_of are written; source, source_url, confidence, unit and note survive.
A change beyond max_change_percent is refused and logged.
as_of never moves backwards, so a lagging upstream cannot downgrade a fresher derived figure.
Long series: a series that fails to fetch is carried forward from the last good run, not dropped.
Long series: a series returning fewer than 90 percent of the stored observations is refused as truncated.
Long series: a run with nothing fetched and nothing stored refuses to write rather than emptying the file.
Long series: every already-published observation an upstream restates is diffed and logged as a revision.
updater.series_note: The long series in series.json are machine-owned and rewritten wholesale, so they follow different rules from the curated figures above: nothing is preserved across a run because nothing there is hand-authored. What is guarded instead is that the file never gets worse than what it replaced. Every series is validated against the econ-core contract at write time and a violation raises rather than being written.

treasury_debt_to_the_penny.note: Sort by -record_date and take the first row. tot_pub_debt_out_amt is in dollars; the stored value is USD trillions.

fred_csv.note: Keyless CSV fallback. Used when FRED_API_KEY is absent.

statcan_wds.note: Needs vector IDs. Unresolved; see the gap note in the README. Until a vector is confirmed against a published StatCan table, this target stays manual rather than guessed.

nyfed_household_credit.note: Parse the published workbook. Never scrape the HTML page: the layout changes and a scrape fails silently into a plausible wrong number.

fred_series.GFDEGDQ188S: us_debt_to_gdp_total. Total public debt as percent of GDP, quarterly
fred_series.FYGFGDQ188S: us_debt_held_by_public_pct_gdp. US debt held by the public as percent of GDP
fred_series.GDP: us_gdp_nominal. US nominal gross domestic product, quarterly; published in billions, stored in trillions
fred_series.GFDEBTN: us_total_public_debt. Total public debt outstanding, quarterly; published in millions, stored in trillions
fred_series.HDTGPDUSQ163N: us_household_debt_pct_gdp. US household debt as percent of GDP, BIS basis
fred_series.HDTGPDCAQ163N: ca_household_debt_pct_gdp. Canada household debt as percent of GDP, BIS basis
fred_series.TDSP: us_household_debt_service_ratio. US household debt service ratio
fred_series.CDSP: us_consumer_debt_service_ratio. US consumer debt service ratio
fred_series.BCNSDODNS: us_nonfinancial_corporate_debt. US nonfinancial corporate debt securities and loans; published in millions, stored in trillions
fred_series.A091RC1Q027SBEA: us_federal_interest_payments. US federal interest payments; published in billions, stored in trillions
fred_series.POPTHM: us_population. US population, monthly, thousands of persons
fred_series.MKTGDPCAA646NWDB: ca_gdp_nominal_usd. Canada nominal GDP, annual; published in dollars, stored in trillions
fred_series.USREC: Not a series of this app. NBER recession indicator, the source of the US recession bands in recessions.json
fred_series.DEXCAUS: Not a series of this app. Canadian dollars per US dollar, daily; cited by gdp.json

consumed_by.note: The page fetches one composed payload rather than these files directly. The payload is built from disk and cached on the newest mtime here, so a refresh run from host cron is reflected on the next request without restarting the container.
consumed_by.schedule: Host crontab, daily 0615 UTC: docker exec debt-updater python /app/server.py --refresh

fred_series_note: Keys are upstream FRED mnemonics; the value names the econ-core contract id the series is published under in series.json. The two differ deliberately: the overlay site keys on a stable snake_case id, and FRED mnemonics are neither stable nor shared across sources. Where a contract id also names a curated figure it is the same id and the same unit on purpose.
